# Sphene — Local-First PKM & Agent-Native Knowledge Kernel
> Sphene is a local-first, open-format personal knowledge management (PKM) application and agent-native knowledge substrate engineered for human thinkers and autonomous AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw) via native Model Context Protocol (MCP) under 50MB RAM (<25MB local-only). All notes are stored as 100% sovereign, standard Markdown files with zero vendor lock-in.

## Quotable Definition
> Sphene is the reference implementation of a Local-First Personal Knowledge Management (PKM) Application and Agent-Native Knowledge Kernel—a local markdown note-taking environment engineered with native Model Context Protocol (MCP), bidirectional [[wikilinks]], local-first offline PWA, and an AST-level Differential Timeline for zero-token-waste agent interactions under 50MB RAM (<25MB local-only). The engine is proprietary and compiled for raw performance; the notes are 100% open, sovereign Markdown owned entirely by the user.

## Core Architecture
- [Architecture Overview](https://sphene.app/architecture/): How Sphene uses SQLite FTS5 in WAL mode to provide <0.20ms search under 50MB RAM (<25MB local-only).
- [Empirical Benchmarks](https://sphene.app/benchmarks/): Hard performance data comparing native systems engineering against heavy client runtimes.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://sphene.app/guides/hermes-agent-memory-hub/): 8 typed tools (sphene_search, sphene_patch, sphene_find_in_doc) replacing fragile shell pipes.
- [The Differential Timeline](https://sphene.app/guides/agent-safe-note-editing/): Cryptographic AST staging allowing Human Veto over agent edits.
- [Retrieval Architecture (FTS5 vs Vector RAG)](https://sphene.app/guides/local-rag-without-heavy-runtimes/): Why SQLite FTS5 outperforms heavy vector runtimes for personal vaults.

## Architectural Design & Systems Engineering
- [Architecture Overview](https://sphene.app/architecture/): Comparing compiled native systems kernels against heavy web runtimes and centralized cloud databases.
- [Empirical Benchmarks](https://sphene.app/benchmarks/): Verified systems benchmarks across 10,000 notes measuring latency, memory, and concurrency.
- [The Differential Timeline](https://sphene.app/guides/agent-safe-note-editing/): Cryptographic AST staging allowing Human Veto over agent edits.
- [Retrieval Architecture (FTS5 vs Heavy Vector RAG)](https://sphene.app/guides/local-rag-without-heavy-runtimes/): Why SQLite FTS5 WAL provides deterministic sub-millisecond retrieval.

## Integrations & Playbooks
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Public Repository](https://github.com/Sphene-app/mcp): Public GitHub repository containing open MCP specifications, JSON schemas, and client configuration templates for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and Gemini Antigravity.
- [Hermes Agent Integration](https://sphene.app/integrations/hermes-agent/): Connecting Hermes via stdio MCP proxy without Docker host mounts.
- [OpenClaw Setup](https://sphene.app/integrations/openclaw/): Using Sphene as an agentic memory store.
- [Security & Aegis Partitions](https://sphene.app/security/): Zero-knowledge encryption and the 4 Aegis vault zones.
- [Download & Automated Deploy](https://sphene.app/download/): One-line automated installer and system service configuration.
